chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Umara who said:

Hammad ibn Abi Hanifa, when he met me, would say, 'Reiterate your hadith upon me.' So I narrated it saying, 'We are reporting that a worshipper of the Children of Israel, when he reached the peak in worship, became a walker regarding the needs of the people, enduring with what was correct for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intense worship and social service in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the transition from intense individual devotion to active social service, a concept central to Shia ethics where spiritual perfection is measured by one's utility to the community. It illustrates that true *'ibadah* (worship) culminates in becoming a means of relief for others, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of balancing the rights of God and the rights of creation. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khidmah* (service) as an extension of piety, ensuring that devotion does not lead to social isolation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Umara who said,

‘When Hammad Bin Abu Haneefa met me, said, ‘Reiterate your Hadeeth upon me’. So I narrated it saying, ‘We are reporting, ‘It was so that a worshipper of the Children of Israel, when he reached the peak in the worship, became a walker regarding the needs of the people, enduring with what was correct for them’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “Creatures are My dependents. The most beloved among them to Me is the most compassionate of them toward the others and who endeavors the most to help them.’”
